From 41c606879f89623dd5269eaffea640b915e9e17c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Hui Wang <hui.wang@canonical.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Apr 2022 17:43:39 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] Revert "serial: sc16is7xx: Clear RS485 bits in the shutdown"

This reverts commit 927728a34f11b5a27f4610bdb7068317d6fdc72a.

Once the uart_port->rs485->flag is set to SER_RS485_ENABLED, the port
should always work in RS485 mode. If users want the port to leave
RS485 mode, they need to call ioctl() to clear SER_RS485_ENABLED.

So here we shouldn't clear the RS485 bits in the shutdown().

Fixes: 927728a34f11 ("serial: sc16is7xx: Clear RS485 bits in the shutdown")
Signed-off-by: Hui Wang <hui.wang@canonical.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220418094339.678144-1-hui.wang@canonical.com
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/tty/serial/sc16is7xx.c b/drivers/tty/serial/sc16is7xx.c
index e857fb61efbf..5fb201c1b563 100644
--- a/drivers/tty/serial/sc16is7xx.c
+++ b/drivers/tty/serial/sc16is7xx.c
@@ -1238,12 +1238,10 @@ static void sc16is7xx_shutdown(struct uart_port *port)
 
 	/* Disable all interrupts */
 	sc16is7xx_port_write(port, SC16IS7XX_IER_REG, 0);
-	/* Disable TX/RX, clear auto RS485 and RTS invert */
+	/* Disable TX/RX */
 	sc16is7xx_port_update(port, SC16IS7XX_EFCR_REG,
 			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_RXDISABLE_BIT |
-			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_TXDISABLE_BIT |
-			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_AUTO_RS485_BIT |
-			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_RTS_INVERT_BIT,
+			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_TXDISABLE_BIT,
 			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_RXDISABLE_BIT |
 			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_TXDISABLE_BIT);
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/tty/serial/sc16is7xx.c`**
   - The line that clears the RS485 bits during the shutdown process has been removed. Specifically, the following line was modified:
     - Original: 
       ```c
       sc16is7xx_port_update(port, SC16IS7XX_EFCR_REG,
                             SC16IS7XX_EFCR_RXDISABLE_BIT |
                             SC16IS7XX_EFCR_TXDISABLE_BIT |
                             SC16IS7XX_EFCR_AUTO_RS485_BIT |
                             SC16IS7XX_EFCR_RTS_INVERT_BIT,
                             SC16IS7XX_EFCR_RXDISABLE_BIT |
                             SC16IS7XX_EFCR_TXDISABLE_BIT);
       ```
     - Modified:
       ```c
       sc16is7xx_port_update(port, SC16IS7XX_EFCR_REG,
                             SC16IS7XX_EFCR_RXDISABLE_BIT |
                             SC16IS7XX_EFCR_TXDISABLE_BIT,
                             SC16IS7XX_EFCR_RXDISABLE_BIT |
                             SC16IS7XX_EFCR_TXDISABLE_BIT);
       ```

### Relationships

- The patch reverts a previous commit (927728a34f11) that incorrectly modified the shutdown behavior of the RS485 mode in the `sc16is7xx` driver. The change ensures that once the RS485 mode is enabled, it remains active until explicitly disabled by the user through an ioctl call, rather than being cleared during the shutdown process. This modification aligns the driver behavior with the intended functionality of the RS485 mode.

Here is the commit message:
Revert "serial: sc16is7xx: Clear RS485 bits in the shutdown"

This reverts commit 927728a34f11b5a27f4610bdb7068317d6fdc72a.

Once the uart_port->rs485->flag is set to SER_RS485_ENABLED, the port
should always work in RS485 mode. If users want the port to leave
RS485 mode, they need to call ioctl() to clear SER_RS485_ENABLED.

So here we shouldn't clear the RS485 bits in the shutdown().

Fixes: 927728a34f11 ("serial: sc16is7xx: Clear RS485 bits in the shutdown")
Signed-off-by: Hui Wang <hui.wang@canonical.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220418094339.678144-1-hui.wang@canonical.com
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the incorrect handling of the RS485 mode during the shutdown process in the `sc16is7xx` driver. Specifically, the previous implementation cleared the RS485 bits when the shutdown function was called, which led to the unintended disabling of RS485 mode. This behavior contradicted the expected functionality where the RS485 mode should remain enabled until explicitly disabled by the user through an ioctl call.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void sc16is7xx_shutdown(struct uart_port *port)
 {
 	struct sc16is7xx_port *s = dev_get_drvdata(port->dev);
 	struct sc16is7xx_one *one = to_sc16is7xx_one(port, port);
 
 	kthread_cancel_delayed_work_sync(&one->ms_work);
 
 	/* Disable all interrupts */
 	sc16is7xx_port_write(port, SC16IS7XX_IER_REG, 0);
-	/* Disable TX/RX, clear auto RS485 and RTS invert */
+	/* Disable TX/RX */
 	sc16is7xx_port_update(port, SC16IS7XX_EFCR_REG,
 			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_RXDISABLE_BIT |
-			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_TXDISABLE_BIT |
-			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_AUTO_RS485_BIT |
-			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_RTS_INVERT_BIT,
+			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_TXDISABLE_BIT,
 			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_RXDISABLE_BIT |
 			      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_TXDISABLE_BIT);
 
 	sc16is7xx_power(port, 0);
 
 	kthread_flush_worker(&s->kworker);
 }

```c

                      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_RXDISABLE_BIT |
                      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_TXDISABLE_BIT |
                      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_AUTO_RS485_BIT |
                      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_RTS_INVERT_BIT,
                      ...
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the shutdown function incorrectly clears the RS485 bits (specifically `SC16IS7XX_EFCR_AUTO_RS485_BIT`) when the port is shut down. This leads to the RS485 mode being disabled unintentionally, which contradicts the expected behavior that RS485 mode should remain enabled until explicitly disabled by the user.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
sc16is7xx_port_update(port, SC16IS7XX_EFCR_REG,
                      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_RXDISABLE_BIT |
                      SC16IS7XX_EFCR_TXDISABLE_BIT,
                      ...
```
Reason:
The fix removes the clearing of the RS485 bits during the shutdown process, ensuring that the RS485 mode remains enabled as intended. By only disabling the TX and RX without affecting the RS485 settings, the port will continue to operate in RS485 mode until the user explicitly disables it through an ioctl call.
